attempts.summary:
On node1 (RHEL 7.9), installed rootless podman 1.6.4 (via CentOS-7 vault extras/base/updates repos, since RHEL entitlement wasn't available), created the unprivileged appsvc user with a subuid/subgid range, enabled lingering for appsvc, and deployed a containerized nginx web app (docker.io/library/nginx:alpine) as appsvc, port-mapped to 8080. The container is managed by a systemd --user unit (container-webapp.service) enabled under appsvc's user manager, and the user manager itself is enabled to start at system boot (user@1001.service enabled against default.target/multi-user.target) so it runs without appsvc ever having an active login session. Verified this survives an actual node reboot: boot ID changed, appsvc has zero login sessions, user@1001.service and the container-webapp.service came up automatically, and the app returns HTTP 200 on $NODE_IP:8080.

Non-obvious fixes required along the way: restored a missing user@.service systemd template unit (stripped from this image's systemd package), enabled user.max_user_namespaces sysctl, fixed newuidmap/newgidmap capability conflicts, installed missing fuse/fuse3 packages for fuse-overlayfs, worked around a podman rootless bug where the reexec'd child fatally aborts if it can't chdir back to the invoking shell's original (inaccessible) cwd, disabled default seccomp (kernel 3.10 syscall-table mismatch caused nginx's pwrite to fail with EPERM), and replaced the buggy auto-generated Type=forking/PIDFile unit with a reliable Type=simple unit. Discovered that this systemd 219 build's logind does not reliably auto-start lingering users' sessions at boot, so the user@1001.service was additionally enabled directly as a system unit for reliability.
